# Catalyst Growth Coaching and at.theboard, full text

> The full text of https://catalystgrowthcoach.co.uk/board, https://catalystgrowthcoach.co.uk/, the three TeamStrong pages and the two LeadStrong pages for medical devices, as Markdown. See https://catalystgrowthcoach.co.uk/llms.txt for the short version.

# A men’s business group for owner-managers in Milton Keynes

at.theboard is a men’s business group in Milton Keynes for owners running businesses of roughly £500k to £5m with five to twenty-five staff. Five men form a circle and stay together for twelve months. Once a month the circle meets in person at the Shire Retreat for a walk and a half day at the whiteboard, and a fortnight later it meets online for ninety minutes. Every man’s challenge goes on the whiteboard every month, and every man leaves with what he said he would do written up in his own hand, with a date against it. The year is built to change the business: more profit and more of it to you, turnover past where you have stalled, sales that do not all run through you, and a business that needs you less. It is run by John Obidipe of Catalyst Growth Coaching.

## What you turn up to

You set the targets. Four men doing the same make sure you hit them.

Every fortnight, in the circle app before each session, you tell the circle where you have got to with what you set out to do. Every month, you put whatever is pressing on the whiteboard, the five of us work it through, and you leave with the first step written in your own hand. Every few months, the full hour is yours, on the biggest thing you are taking on.

## The session format

### We walk, whatever the weather (60 min)

All five of you and me, outdoors. You change who you walk beside so you speak to everyone. Saying the hard thing is easier when nobody is looking at your face.

### Coffee is waiting (On arrival)

It is ordered ahead and delivered to the room, so nobody loses twenty minutes to a queue. The walk loosens the thinking, the room finishes it.

### One man, the full hour (60 min)

The biggest thing he is taking on goes up and stays there until it has a shape and a first step he can take on Monday. He writes that step on the whiteboard himself before he sits down. The full hour comes round to each man roughly every five months.

### Then two men, half an hour each (60 min)

Whatever is pressing. Half an hour gets somewhere when four men already know your business, and it ends the same way, with a line in your handwriting and a date against it.

### A fortnight later, online (90 min)

The first half hour is all five of you saying where you have got to with what you wrote on the board last time. Four times a year this half hour becomes the numbers round. Then two men take half an hour each on the board.

### Just you and me (90 min, every 2 months)

Ninety minutes with the whiteboard, for whatever you are not ready to say in front of the other four yet. I also tell you the pattern I have seen in your decisions since we last sat down.

Every man is on the board every month. The full hour is yours roughly every five months.

## The rules of the circle

Six rules, and they are the reason it works. Every man signs up to the same ones before his first session.

### You turn up

Twice a month, for twelve months. Not when it suits, and not only when the weather is good.

### You bring something real

Not the summary. The thing you have been going round in the car.

### You do what you said, or say why not

The first half hour of every online session is exactly this.

### You wait your turn at the board

The first part of every slot is the man on the board and me, questions only. Then the floor opens and you come in. Nobody jumps in early, and I hold the line on it.

### You keep it in the room

All of it. That is what makes the rest possible.

### If a man is coasting, the other four say so

Out loud, in the room, before I have to.

> Four men who will hold you to what you said, and never repeat a word of it outside the room.

### If you drift

Miss commitments without saying why and you and I talk before the next session. Keep drifting and you step out. You stop paying and go back on the waiting list. Your seat goes to the next man waiting, so the other four keep a circle of five. A missed commitment with an honest reason does not count.

## Who runs it

John Obidipe runs at.theboard. He has spent more than fifteen years in consulting and executive coaching. He has coached leaders inside Toyota, Convatec and the University of Oxford, and owners running firms of £500k to £5m. He is Gallup-certified in CliftonStrengths, a questionnaire that shows how each person thinks and works best. Every member takes CliftonStrengths when he joins.

I will not tell you how to run your business. What I will do is bring what I have seen work and fail in other companies, large and small. Then we find the answer together, rather than me handing you one.

> There is no good reason to solve something with one mind when you can put six on it.

> “The pressure and expectation isn't solely on me. I'm not standing there having to find a way through these problems alone.”Mark Schmull , MD, Arrow Planning

## What owners ask before they join

### Is there a men’s business group in Milton Keynes?

Yes. at.theboard is a circle of five male owner-managers in Milton Keynes who meet in person every month at the Shire Retreat and online a fortnight later, for twelve months. It is a business peer group for owners who want to be pushed on their numbers and their decisions, rather than a social or wellbeing group.

### Who is it for?

Men who own and run a business in or near Milton Keynes, usually with £500k to £5m turnover and five to twenty-five staff, who are still doing a lot of the work themselves and want four other owners holding them to what they say they will do. Smaller businesses are welcome to book the free hour and talk.

### How often does the circle meet?

Twice a month. One in-person half day at the Shire Retreat: a sixty-minute walk, coffee, then the whiteboard, where one man takes a full hour and two men take half an hour each. A fortnight later, ninety minutes online. Each member also has ninety minutes one to one with John every two months. That comes to about six hours a month.

### What does a year in the circle change?

The business, in figures you already track: profit and what you take home, turnover past the point where you have stalled, sales that no longer all run through you, a business that can run without you for a fortnight, and what it would be worth to a buyer. Each man writes down at joining what the year has to be worth to him, and the circle holds him to it in month seven and month thirteen.

### How long do I commit for?

Twelve months. The circle stays the same five men for the year, because the value comes from people who know your business well enough to notice when you are coasting.

### How much does it cost?

£550 a month for members of the first circle, held at that rate for as long as they stay. Later circles pay more. Month thirteen and the quarterly Reset day are priced separately at cost.

### How is this different from a networking group?

Networking groups in Milton Keynes meet weekly or fortnightly to pass referrals. at.theboard has no referral target and no selling in the room. Five owners work on each other’s real decisions, and every commitment is written on the whiteboard with a name and a date.

### How does it compare with Vistage or The Alternative Board?

Both are established peer advisory options. Vistage groups usually have twelve to sixteen members meeting for a day each month, and The Alternative Board runs monthly advisory boards in Milton Keynes. at.theboard is smaller, five men, with every member on the whiteboard every month, a walk built into each session, and a fixed twelve-month circle.

### How do I join?

Start with a free hour at the whiteboard with John on whatever is live in your business. The free hour is open to anyone. A place in a circle is not. If a circle is right for you, you go on a waiting list until John can place you in one where nobody does what you do. The first circle is being selected now.

[How at.theboard compares with the other options in Milton Keynes](https://catalystgrowthcoach.co.uk/business-groups-milton-keynes)

## Location

In person at the Shire Retreat, Milton Keynes. Online between sessions. Members will come from across Milton Keynes and the surrounding area.

## How to join

Online, or in person in Milton Keynes. Your choice.

### It goes on the whiteboard

Whatever is live this week, in your words, not the tidy version.

### You leave with something to do

We stay with it until it has a shape and something you can act on Monday.

### No pitch afterwards

Free whether you join or not. No follow-up sequence.

I say what I think as we go rather than saving it up for the end. That includes telling you if what you have is a process problem rather than a judgement one. If it is, I will say so and send you off to fix the process. That happens, and it costs me the work, which is fine.

Book the free hour: https://catalystgrowthcoach.co.uk/board#book

# Catalyst Growth Coaching, home page

Strategic thinking, out loud, at a whiteboard. Another mind in the room with you. For senior leaders.

> The first word goes on the board. Everything that matters happens after that.

Nothing in your week is designed for thinking.

Meetings are designed for decisions. Email is designed for response. The calendar is designed for time-blocking. Your assistant is designed for protection.

Every system around you is optimising for output. None of them are optimising for thought.

The result: you make decisions in the cracks. You arrive at the most important meeting of your quarter without having actually sat with the question. You leave the most expensive moments of your week to be navigated by reflex.

Whiteboard Sessions are the thing the rest of your week is incompatible with.

## A Whiteboard Session is what it sounds like, with one thing the name doesn't tell you. You're not thinking alone.

You arrive. The board is empty. We start with whatever's actually live for you, and we think it through together, out loud, until it's clear. I'm not there to watch you work. I'm the other mind in the room, asking the question you'd stopped asking, catching the thing you've gone blind to because you see it every day.

Sometimes that takes an hour. Sometimes three. The work is finished when the question is answered, when the next move is clear, the decision made.

Your thinking, out of your head, onto the board, into a solution.

## Three things, mostly.

The strategic question you've been carrying without having sat with. The thing you keep meaning to think about but haven't.

The mid-altitude problem that's stuck. Where the system is producing the wrong output and you can't see where the leverage is.

The tactical decision you've been over-thinking. Where you know what to do but haven't given yourself permission to do it.

These are the three altitudes. Most weeks have at least one of them building up. We find which one needs the work, and we think it through together.

Working with John has been transformative. I came in overwhelmed and stuck; I left with a clear structure for how I lead and make decisions under pressure.

Working with John has given me renewed focus and confidence at a point in my career when I really needed it. The CliftonStrengths work was the most clarifying thing I have done professionally.

I just wish I had met John years ago. The frameworks he uses would have saved me from expensive mistakes in two previous businesses.

Who John is Fifteen years across organisational consulting and executive coaching. Gallup certified in CliftonStrengths and a FITT16 practitioner, the 16-type profile built from it. [The credentials in full](https://catalystgrowthcoach.co.uk/about)

Who John works with Alongside the organisations above, individual leaders coached from AWS, Volkswagen Financial Services, Nexans and Bassett Mechanical, among others, across industries and countries. [What the work looks like in the room](https://catalystgrowthcoach.co.uk/in-practice)

## Three contexts. Same practice.

The fastest way to know if this is for you is to be at the board for an hour.

You'll know whether the practice fits you.

One hour. No charge, nothing to prepare.

# Good is where your leaders are. It is not where they have to stop, on their own or together.

Some leadership teams run the business together. Others are a group of leaders who each run their own part of it and come together to report. Both can grow, in different ways. Choose the one that sounds like you.

## We run the business together.

You share the decisions and the outcomes, and you want to work as one.

[For teams who work as one](https://catalystgrowthcoach.co.uk/teamstrong/one-team)

## We each run our own area.

You lead your own region, function or division, and you want every leader to grow in how they lead it.

[For leaders who run their own area](https://catalystgrowthcoach.co.uk/teamstrong/leaders)

## Start with a conversation

Book a conversation: https://catalystgrowthcoach.co.uk/teamstrong#book

<!-- canonical: https://catalystgrowthcoach.co.uk/teamstrong/one-team -->

# “Everyone around the table is capable. We still do not work as one.”

For leadership teams of five to ten who share the decisions, the pressure and the outcomes. I find out how your team really works, through the lens that suits you best. Then we work through what it shows you, at the board, until it changes how you lead together.

## You know this team is better than it performs

> “We agree in the meeting, and by Thursday nothing has moved.”

> “I know who is strongest at what. I am not sure they do.”

> “We are polite with each other, and I think the politeness is costing us.”

> “Some days I am sure it is that person over there. Other days I wonder if it is me.”

## There is more than one way to see how a team really works

Ask a leadership team how they work together and you will hear how they would like to work. To see how they actually work, you need to look from the outside, through more than one lens, and I choose the one that fits your team. Whichever we use, every session looks at both sides: how the team works together, and how its leader shows up.

## One day your team will still be talking about months later

A single, high impact day at your venue or ours, in the setting you choose. Each leads to the same place: a clear, shared picture of how you really work as a team, and two or three changes you agree before you leave.

### The construction site.

A working miniature construction site, six metres by three, brought to your venue. Your team operates the machines to complete a set task together. Within minutes the patterns show themselves: who communicates, who plans, who is strongest at which job, and what happens when the plan meets the ground.

### The board.

Your team brings a live problem it has not been able to settle, and we work it through together at the whiteboard until it is resolved. How you reach the answer tells you as much as the answer itself.

### The strengths lens.

Everyone completes FITT16 and CliftonStrengths beforehand. On the day the whole team’s profile goes on the board, so each person sees why they work the way they do, and why the person next to them works differently.

From £3,500 plus VAT for a leadership team, priced on numbers. One price, with everything included.

## When the change has to last

One high impact session a month, each in a different setting, so the team keeps moving. The mix is chosen for your team. A typical shape:

- Month one, the construction site.The team as it is today.
- Month two, the strengths lens.Why it works that way.
- Months three to five, the board.Real decisions, worked through together, with actions and dates checked each month.
- Month six, back to the construction site.The same task, the same team, and a very different result.

The leader has their own one-to-one sessions alongside. Price agreed with each team.

## Questions

### What space does the construction site need?

Two areas side by side: one for the construction site, which is six metres by three, and one for horseshoe seating where we talk. It works indoors or outdoors, and the machines are self-powered, so no power is needed.

### What if someone would rather not drive the machines?

That is fine. There is plenty to do without driving, and planning the task is often where the most revealing conversations happen.

### What is included in the price?

Everything. The Day is one price for the whole package, construction site included, from £3,500 plus VAT depending on numbers. For the Six Months, we agree one price before we start, and it includes the one-to-one sessions.

### Do we have to use the construction site?

No. The construction site is one of three settings, alongside the board and the strengths lens. We choose together what suits your team.

## Start with a conversation

Tell me about your team and what you would like to see change. A short conversation is enough to work out whether the Day, the Six Months or neither is the right fit.

Book a conversation: https://catalystgrowthcoach.co.uk/teamstrong/one-team#book

<!-- canonical: https://catalystgrowthcoach.co.uk/teamstrong/leaders -->

# “We spend the meeting on the numbers. The real story is in how we lead.”

For leadership teams of five to ten where each leader runs their own region, function or division. You are not trying to become one team. Each of you is growing in how you lead your own people, and you are doing it alongside each other.

## Everyone reports on their team. Nobody reports on themselves.

### If you sit around the table

> “I know exactly how my numbers are doing. I am less sure how I am doing.”

> “My team takes its lead from me. I am not always sure what it is taking.”

> “I can see what is not working in my area. I am less sure how much of it starts with me.”

### If you lead the leaders, or look after them

> “Some of my leaders are further along than others. We all know it, and nobody says it.”

> “I want every one of my leaders to grow, each at their own level. This is how I invest in all of them at once, and nobody is singled out.”

## A clearer view of how each of you leads

It is hard to see how you lead from inside your own area. So we step outside it together and look from a different angle, one that shows each of you how you come across to the people who report to you. Each leader leaves knowing what they want to change.

## One day, and every leader takes something back to their team

A single, high impact day at your venue or ours, in the setting you choose. Each leader leaves with a clear picture of how they show up, and two or three changes to take back to their own team.

### The construction site.

A working miniature construction site, six metres by three, brought to your venue. You operate the machines to complete a set task together, and each leader’s habits show up within minutes: how they plan, how they communicate, when they step in and when they let go.

### The board.

Each leader brings a live challenge from their own area, and we work it through at the whiteboard with the rest of the group as a second set of minds. Everyone learns from everyone else’s problem.

### The strengths lens.

Everyone completes FITT16 and CliftonStrengths beforehand. On the day each leader sees why they lead the way they do, and what that means for the people who report to them.

From £3,500 plus VAT for a leadership team, priced on numbers. One price, with everything included.

## Each leader growing, month by month

One high impact session a month, each in a different setting, so the growth keeps moving and has time to show up in each leader’s own team. The mix is chosen for your leaders. A typical shape:

- Month one, the construction site.How each of you leads today.
- Month two, the strengths lens.Why you lead that way.
- Months three to five, the board.Real challenges from each area, with actions and dates checked each month.
- Month six, back to the construction site.The same task, and a clear view of how each of you has changed.

Leaders can have their own one-to-one sessions alongside where it helps. Price agreed with each team.

## Questions

### What space does the construction site need?

Two areas side by side: one for the construction site, which is six metres by three, and one for horseshoe seating where we talk. It works indoors or outdoors, and the machines are self-powered, so no power is needed.

### What if someone would rather not drive the machines?

That is fine. There is plenty to do without driving, and planning the task is often where the most revealing conversations happen.

### What is included in the price?

Everything. The Day is one price for the whole package, construction site included, from £3,500 plus VAT depending on numbers. For the Six Months, we agree one price before we start, and it includes the one-to-one sessions.

### Our leaders do not work together day to day. Will this still work?

Yes, that is exactly who this page is for. The aim is not to make you one team. It is for each leader to see how they lead their own people, with the others alongside.

## Start with a conversation

Tell me about your leaders and what you would like to see grow. A short conversation is enough to work out whether the Day, the Six Months or neither is the right fit.

Book a conversation: https://catalystgrowthcoach.co.uk/teamstrong/leaders#book

# Everyone around the table is capable. You want to be the one whose judgement they trust.

One-to-one coaching at the whiteboard for vice presidents in medical device companies who are ready for the next seat, whether that is general manager, a regional leadership role or the executive committee. I currently work with senior leaders at Convatec, Urgo and Becton Dickinson.

## You are trusted to deliver. You want to be trusted to decide.

“At this level performance is assumed. What people notice now is how I think when the pressure is on.”

“Global wants delivery, my directors want answers, and there are very few people I can think out loud with.”

“When a restructure or a portfolio call goes against my region, I keep everyone steady and carry the cost quietly.”

“Too much still comes back to me. I want directors who grow the business without needing me in every decision.”

“Most of what I have tried on leadership was written for people earlier in their careers than I am.”

“I spend so much time on this quarter that the thinking about the next five years keeps getting pushed back.”

## Leading at the level you know you are capable of

You want a seat where your decisions shape the direction of the business, and a reputation in the executive room as someone whose view is sought before the decision is made. You want a bench of directors strong enough that the growth in your region comes from the leaders you have developed as much as from the deals they close. And you want enough clear space to think about where the business is going, so that this quarter informs your decisions without running them.

## Your thinking, out of your head and onto the whiteboard

Each session starts with whatever is live for you that week, whether that is a board presentation, a difficult director, a portfolio decision or the role you are working towards. It all goes up on the whiteboard, and we work through each issue until you leave with a decision, an action and a date. At the next session we check every one, so nothing slips.

I ask questions first, because the answer is usually already in your thinking and the whiteboard lets you see it. When it helps, I give you my honest view as well. Sessions run online with the whiteboard shared live on screen, or in person. Where a company wants it, I travel to the team.

## Senior leaders at Convatec, Urgo and Becton Dickinson

I work with directors and vice presidents across three of the sector’s leading medical device companies, in the UK and across Europe. I understand the pressures of the role at this level: a global matrix, a number that never goes away, NHS and hospital customers asking for more value, and a career that depends on how you are seen as much as what you deliver.

I have also written at length about the move from vice president to the C-suite in my LinkedIn newsletter, so you can read how I think before we ever meet.

I am John Obidipe, an executive coach with more than fifteen years in organisational consulting and coaching. I am Gallup-certified in CliftonStrengths and a FITT16 practitioner, and I use both to show you how you lead at your best and where pressure pulls you away from it.

### Six months, a fixed end date.

We agree two or three outcomes you can measure at the start.

### A decision every session.

You leave with actions and dates, and we check them next time.

### My honest view.

Questions first, then a straight answer when you want one.

### Strictly confidential.

What you bring stays between us, including when your company is paying.

The price. Six months, a session a week, about 24 sessions in all, for £7,200. If you would rather stop at the halfway point, three months costs £3,600. Many vice presidents have this funded by their company, and I am happy to speak with your sponsor or L&D team.

## One free hour at the whiteboard

Bring whatever is most live for you right now. We will work on it properly for an hour, and at the end you will know whether working together makes sense. There is no sales conversation and no obligation.

Book a free hour: https://catalystgrowthcoach.co.uk/mdsvp#book

# You deliver the number every year. You want to be known for where the business goes next.

One-to-one coaching at the whiteboard for sales directors in medical device companies who are working towards vice president. I currently work with senior leaders at Convatec, Urgo and Becton Dickinson.

## Strong results, and the next role still feels a step away

“When my VP asks where the business should go, I hear myself answering with the forecast.”

“My managers bring every difficult decision to me, so I never have time to think beyond this quarter.”

“Global wants certainty, the NHS accounts want more value for less money, and I am the one holding it together.”

“I am good at keeping everything steady. I am less sure that is what gets people promoted.”

“I have done the leadership programme. It explained the theory but did not change how I handle a Tuesday when everything lands at once.”

“I want the VP role, and I want to be ready before it is offered.”

## Stepping into vice president ready

You want to walk into the VP role already leading at that level, with a team of managers who make good decisions without you and a reputation as someone who thinks about the whole business. You want the confidence to put your own view on the table first, in front of your VP and the global team, and to have it taken seriously. And you want to close the gap between how you are seen today and the leader you know you can be.

## Your thinking, out of your head and onto the whiteboard

Each session starts with whatever is live for you that week, whether that is a forecast review, a manager who keeps escalating, a key account under pressure or the case you are building for promotion. It all goes up on the whiteboard, and we work through each issue until you leave with a decision, an action and a date. At the next session we check every one, so nothing slips.

I ask questions first, because the answer is usually already in your thinking and the whiteboard lets you see it. When it helps, I give you my honest view as well. Sessions run online with the whiteboard shared live on screen, or in person.

## Senior leaders at Convatec, Urgo and Becton Dickinson

I work with directors and vice presidents across three of the sector’s leading medical device companies, in the UK and across Europe. I understand the pressures of the role: targets set a long way from the field, hospital and NHS customers asking for more value, and a career that depends on how you are seen as much as what you deliver.

I have also written at length about the move from director to vice president in my LinkedIn newsletter, so you can read how I think before we ever meet.

I am John Obidipe, an executive coach with more than fifteen years in organisational consulting and coaching. I am Gallup-certified in CliftonStrengths and a FITT16 practitioner, and I use both to show you how you lead at your best and where pressure pulls you away from it.

### Six months, a fixed end date.

We agree two or three outcomes you can measure at the start.

You leave with actions and dates, and we check them next time.

Questions first, then a straight answer when you want one.

What you bring stays between us, including when your company is paying.
